target_customer: Mainstream computer users, with developers as the platform audience
problem: Desktop files and web information lived in separate worlds; the founders wanted a web-style layer that merged the two and made common tasks more intuitive.
business_model: Unlaunched platform and applications; no revenue model disclosed
product_category: Web operating system / desktop and web platform

technical_complexity.rationale: A web OS bridging desktop files and web content was ambitious, but the founders were Firefox veterans. Product never launched, so difficulty was not proven.

defensibility.rationale: Unlaunched; the main asset was the team. Several web OS projects already existed and none had a structural moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Facebook bought the company in July 2007 as its first acquisition and put the founders on Facebook Platform work. One outlet repeated a rumor of a Google bid, unconfirmed.

market_need_then: Web OS projects were a hot topic in 2006 and the Firefox founders drew press (IEEE Spectrum cover, blog coverage), but no source shows measured customer demand.

identity.logo: A logo image existed on 2006 coverage; design not described in sources

branding.community_and_virality: Press attention came from the founders' Firefox fame rather than the brand.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand evidence beyond founder reputation; the product never reached users.

outcome_analysis: Parakey was a pre-launch team bet. Blake Ross and Joe Hewitt, known for Firefox, built a web OS concept with Sequoia seed money, and Facebook acquired the company on 2007-07-19 as its first acquisition, with the founders moving to Facebook Platform and site work. The exit reflects founder pedigree and acquihire logic more than product traction.
notes: Dead site, no website listed. Seed date conflicts: YC page says Sequoia seeded in early 2005 while founding is early 2006, so the date is null. Seed amount not found; Crunchbase shows a seed round without a visible amount. Deal price undisclosed. TechCrunch dates founding to 2005. Competitor entries are dated near late 2006, after the YC W07 batch was set; none confirmed as direct rivals since Parakey never launched.
